questions.stem: When medical student were performing the amphibian experiments, they recorded a graph of a muscle contraction, in which latent period: 10ms, contraction period 40ms and relaxation period was 20ms. Calculate tetanizing frequency.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) 25 Hz

questions.stemHtml: While studying the effect of varying the extracellular concentration on the transport rate of a substance, the graph below was obtained. This finding would suggest that this substance is transported by:
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Simple diffusion

questions.stem: In a patient with gastrointestinal symptoms, the dysfunction of which cellular structure, associated with the transmembrane protein Claudin, could potentially lead to altered permeability and paracellular transport?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Tight Junctions

questions.stem: In a study, researchers were assessing the efficacy of the baroreceptor reflex in maintaining blood pressure homeostasis. A healthy volunteer undergoes a positional change from lying to standing, resulting in an initial drop in systolic blood pressure by 20 mm Hg. Subsequently, the baroreceptor reflex partially compensates, restoring 16 mm Hg. What is the gain of the baroreceptor system in this scenario?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) -4

questions.stem: Fick's law of diffusion is dependent on all except:

options.label: C
options.text: The molecular weight of the gas

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) The posture of the subject

questions.stem: Where are lipid rafts typically observed?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Plasma membrane

questions.stem: Gap junctions are intercellular connections that?

options.label: A
options.text: Primarily serve to keep cells separated and allow for transport across a tissue barrier.

options.label: B
options.text: Serve as a regulated cytoplasmic bridge for sharing of small molecules between cells.

options.label: C
options.text: Serve as a barrier to prevent protein movement within the cellular membrane.

options.label: D
options.text: Are cellular components for constitutive exocytosis that occurs between adjacent cells

questions.answerText: Serve as a regulated cytoplasmic bridge for sharing of small molecules between cells.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Serve as a regulated cytoplasmic bridge for sharing of small molecules between cells.

questions.stem: Which of the following physiological processes is not correctly paired with a structure? Electrical transmission: Gap junctionNegative feedback inhibition: Renshaw cellSynaptic vesicle docking and fusion: Presynaptic nerve terminalEnd plate potential: Muscarinic cholinergic receptorAction potential generation: Initial segment
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) 4 only

questions.stemHtml: In a given figure, at which labelled point on the action potential the absolute refractory period is located?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) 2 & 3

questions.stem: Which of the following types of stimuli produces only a local potential, but not an action potential?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Subthreshhold

questions.stem: Which statement is true about the Nernst equation?

options.label: C
options.text: Nernst potential for Cl– is –90 mV

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Used to calculate equilibrium potential

questions.stemHtml: In the experiment illustrated in part A of Figure 2, equal volumes of solutions X, Y, and Z are placed into the compartments of the two U-shaped vessels shown. The two compartments of each vessel are separated by semipermeable membranes (i.e., impermeable to ions and large polar molecules). Part B illustrates the fluid distribution across the membranes at equilibration. Assuming complete dissociation, identify each of the solutions shown.

options.label: A
options.text: Solution X: 1 M CaCl₂ | Solution Y: 1 M NaCl | Solution Z: 1 M glucose

options.label: B
options.text: Solution X: 1 M glucose | Solution Y: 1 M NaCl | Solution Z: 1 M CaCl₂

options.label: C
options.text: Solution X: 1 M NaCl | Solution Y: 2 M glucose | Solution Z: 3 M CaCl₂

options.label: D
options.text: Solution X: 2 M NaCl | Solution Y: 1 M NaCl | Solution Z: Pure water

questions.answerText: Solution X: 1 M glucose | Solution Y: 1 M NaCl | Solution Z: 1 M CaCl₂
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Solution X: 1 M glucose | Solution Y: 1 M NaCl | Solution Z: 1 M CaCl₂

questions.stemHtml: Identify the correct labeling (A, B, C, D respectively) in the given image?

options.label: A
options.text: Z line, A band, H zone, I Band

options.label: B
options.text: A band, Z line, H zone, M Band

options.label: C
options.text: A band, I Band, Z line, H zone

options.label: D
options.text: Z line, A band, M Band, H zone

questions.answerText: Z line, A band, H zone, I Band
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Z line, A band, H zone, I Band

questions.stem: Statement A: The deep and visceral pain are better localized compared to the superficial pain Statement B: There will be a deficiency of A delta fibers in the deep structures compared to superficial structures Which of the following is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The statement A is true, the statement B is false

options.label: B
options.text: The statement A is false, the statement B is true

options.label: C
options.text: Both the statements A and B are true

options.label: D
options.text: Both the statements A and B are false

questions.answerText: The statement A is false, the statement B is true
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) The statement A is false, the statement B is true

questions.stem: A 35-year-old male undergoes surgery under general anesthesia with halothane. Shortly after induction, he develops severe skeletal muscle rigidity, a rapid increase in body temperature & signs of metabolic acidosis indicating Malignant hyperthermia Which of the following molecular changes could account for these clinical manifestations?

options.label: A
options.text: Decreased voltage sensitivity of the dihydropyridine receptor

options.label: B
options.text: Enhanced activity of the sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ ATPase

options.label: C
options.text: Prolonged opening of the ryanodine receptor channel

options.label: D
options.text: Reduction in the density of voltage-sensitive Na+ channels in the T tubule membrane

questions.answerText: Prolonged opening of the ryanodine receptor channel
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Prolonged opening of the ryanodine receptor channel

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man is participating in a study on skeletal muscle physiology. During muscle fiber stimulation, which of the following represents the correct sequence of events involved in excitation-contraction coupling in skeletal muscle?

options.label: A
options.text: Action potential in muscle fiber → Neuromuscular junction activation → Calcium release → T-tubule activation → Contraction

options.label: B
options.text: Neuromuscular junction activation → Action potential in muscle fiber → T-tubule propagation → Calcium release from cisternae → Contraction

options.label: C
options.text: Calcium binds to actin → Action potential spreads → Calcium release → Neuromuscular stimulation → Muscle contracts

options.label: D
options.text: Action potential in T-tubule → Muscle contraction → Calcium release → Action potential in cisternae → Relaxation

questions.answerText: Neuromuscular junction activation → Action potential in muscle fiber → T-tubule propagation → Calcium release from cisternae → Contraction
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Neuromuscular junction activation → Action potential in muscle fiber → T-tubule propagation → Calcium release from cisternae → Contraction

questions.stem: Weber–Fechner law is related to:
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Intensity of stimulus

questions.stem: In which muscles are white fibers predominantly found?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Hand muscles

questions.stemHtml: Which is correct about the pressure volume loop of left ventricle?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Aortic valve opens at 5

questions.stem: A 28-year-old male presents to emergency with severe sudden-onset heart palpitations. The patient reports symptoms of chest pain, fatigue, and dizziness. Upon examination, his heart rate is 165/min and regular. His blood pressure is 106/74 mmHg. A gentle massage below the level of the left mandible elicits an immediate improvement in the patient, as his heart rate returns to 60/min. What was the mechanism of action of this manoeuvre?

options.label: A
options.text: Increasing the refractory period in ventricular myocytes

options.label: B
options.text: Increasing sympathetic tone in systemic arteries

options.label: C
options.text: Decreasing the firing rate of carotid baroreceptors

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Slowing conduction in AV node

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with longstanding uncontrolled hypertension presents with exertional dyspnea. Echocardiogram shows concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Which of the following changes would most likely be observed in his left ventricular pressure-volume loop?

options.label: A
options.text: Decreased end-systolic pressure and increased stroke volume

options.label: B
options.text: Shift of the loop upward and to the right with increased end-diastolic volume

options.label: C
options.text: Increased end-systolic pressure with decreased end-diastolic volume

options.label: D
options.text: Downward shift of the loop with increased compliance

questions.answerText: Increased end-systolic pressure with decreased end-diastolic volume
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Increased end-systolic pressure with decreased end-diastolic volume

questions.stem: The ratio of stroke volume and arterial compliance approximately determines which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Pulse pressure

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man is undergoing a cardiovascular stress test. During exercise, his oxygen consumption increases significantly, leading to an enhanced cardiac output and redistribution of blood flow. Which of the following changes is least likely to occur in response to the increased metabolic demand?

options.label: A
options.text: Increased venous return due to muscle pump action

options.label: B
options.text: Decreased splanchnic blood flow due to sympathetic vasoconstriction

options.label: C
options.text: Increased coronary blood flow mediated by local metabolic vasodilation

options.label: D
options.text: Increased total peripheral resistance (TPR) due to widespread vasoconstriction

questions.answerText: Increased total peripheral resistance (TPR) due to widespread vasoconstriction
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Increased total peripheral resistance (TPR) due to widespread vasoconstriction

questions.stem: Baroreceptors are associated with which vessel and its layer?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Internal carotid artery, adventitial layer

questions.stem: In a clinical research trial two medical students, Sonali & Mitali, were tasked with demonstrating the effect of the sinus nerve on blood pressure regulation during induced hypovolemic shock in canines. Sonali severed the sinus nerve at a mean blood pressure (MBP) of 85 mmHg, while Mitali did the same when the MBP was 50 mmHg. Following the severance of the sinus nerve:

options.label: A
options.text: Sonali observed an increase in MBP, but Mitali noted a decrease in MBP.

options.label: B
options.text: Sonali noted a decrease in MBP, but Mitali observed an increase in MBP.

options.label: C
options.text: Both Sonali and Mitali recorded an increase in MBP.

options.label: D
options.text: Both Sonali and Mitali recorded a decrease in MBP.

questions.answerText: Sonali observed an increase in MBP, but Mitali noted a decrease in MBP.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Sonali observed an increase in MBP, but Mitali noted a decrease in MBP.

questions.stem: During Exercise the cardiac output rises upto 5 times, but pulmonary vascular resistance only few mm Hg. Why?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Opening of parallel channels

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true about the absolute refractory period in the ventricles, except

options.label: A
options.text: Is the period when the ventricles are completely inexcitable.

options.label: B
options.text: Corresponds to the period of ventricular depolarization.

options.label: C
options.text: Corresponds approximately to the period of ventricular contraction.

options.label: D
options.text: Is shorter than the corresponding period in atrial muscle.

questions.answerText: Is shorter than the corresponding period in atrial muscle.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Is shorter than the corresponding period in atrial muscle.

questions.stem: The third heart sound (S3), which may be heard during auscultation in some clinical conditions, is produced by:

options.label: B
options.text: Closure of the semilunar valves (aortic and pulmonary valves)

options.label: C
options.text: Closure of the atrioventricular valves (mitral and tricuspid valves)

options.label: D
options.text: Rapid filling phase of the ventricles

questions.answerText: Rapid filling phase of the ventricles
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Rapid filling phase of the ventricles

questions.stem: Which of the following accurately describes the cardiovascular regulation?

options.label: A
options.text: Baroreceptors get activated in hypotension and help increase Blood pressure

options.label: B
options.text: Baroreceptors inhibit the nucleus ambiguous which inhibits the sympathetic system

options.label: C
options.text: Nucleus tractus solitarius activates vagal centres

options.label: D
options.text: Vagus nerve carries afferent fibres from carotid sinus baroreceptors

questions.answerText: Nucleus tractus solitarius activates vagal centres
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Nucleus tractus solitarius activates vagal centres

questions.stem: Arterioles offer more resistance to flow than other vessels since they have:

options.label: D
options.text: A greater pressure drop along their length.

questions.answerText: A greater pressure drop along their length.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) A greater pressure drop along their length.

questions.stemHtml: Curve B in the figure represents:
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Ventricular volume

questions.stem: During a routine pulmonary assessment of a healthy individual at rest, it is noted that at one specific lung volume, no respiratory muscle activity is required to maintain lung inflation. At this point, the inward elastic recoil of the lungs is perfectly balanced by the outward recoil of the chest wall, resulting in a state of mechanical equilibrium. Which of the following lung volumes corresponds to this condition?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Functional Residual Capacity

questions.stem: In regional ventilation and perfusion of the lung, which of the following is correct:

options.label: A
options.text: Upper regions of the lung ventilate better than the lower regions

options.label: B
options.text: Lower regions of the lung perfuse better than the Upper regions

options.label: C
options.text: V/Q ratio increases down the lung

options.label: D
options.text: The highest alveolar PO2, is at the apex of the lung.

questions.answerText: Lower regions of the lung perfuse better than the Upper regions
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Lower regions of the lung perfuse better than the Upper regions

questions.stem: Pulmonary compliance:

options.label: B
options.text: Is defined as the change in pressure per unit change in volume.

options.label: C
options.text: Compliance is slightly greater when measured during deflation than when measured during inflation

questions.answerText: Compliance is slightly greater when measured during deflation than when measured during inflation
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Compliance is slightly greater when measured during deflation than when measured during inflation

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve are correct?

options.label: A
options.text: A rightward shift of the curve indicates increased affinity of hemoglobin for oxygen, promoting loading of the oxygen loading on Hemoglobin.

options.label: B
options.text: Increased 2,3-DPG levels shift the dissociation curve to the left, enhancing oxygen binding.

options.label: C
options.text: Stored blood (banked blood) may show a left shift due to decreased levels of 2,3-DPG.

options.label: D
options.text: Hypothermia causes a right shift in the oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve.

questions.answerText: Stored blood (banked blood) may show a left shift due to decreased levels of 2,3-DPG.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Stored blood (banked blood) may show a left shift due to decreased levels of 2,3-DPG.

questions.stem: Which one of the following definitions is incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: The respiratory minute volume equals the amount of air inspired per minute.

options.label: B
options.text: Residual volume is the air left in the lungs after a maximal expiratory effort

options.label: C
options.text: Vital capacity is the maximal amount of air that can be expired after a normal inspiration

options.label: D
options.text: Physiological dead space is the amount of air not equilibrating with blood.

questions.answerText: Vital capacity is the maximal amount of air that can be expired after a normal inspiration
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Vital capacity is the maximal amount of air that can be expired after a normal inspiration.

questions.stemHtml: A 27-year-old man is breathing quietly. He then inhales as much air as possible and exhales as much air as he can, producing the spirogram shown in the figure. What is his expiratory reserve volume (in liters)?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) 2.0

questions.stem: How does the Bohr effect operate in myoglobin compared to hemoglobin?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) No Bohr effect

questions.stemHtml: A 65-year-old man with a 40-pack-year smoking history presents with progressive shortness of breath and chronic productive cough. He complains of exertional dyspnea that has worsened over the past year. Pulmonary function testing is performed, and his flow-volume loop (in blue color) is shown below. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis based on the flow-volume pattern and clinical findings?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

questions.stemHtml: Which one of the following curve shows oxygen Hb dissociation after anaerobic exercise
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) C

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true, except, In normal lungs:

options.label: A
options.text: The rate of alveolar ventilation at rest exceeds the rate of alveolar capillary perfusion.

options.label: B
options.text: The ventilation/perfusion (V/P) ratio exceeds 1.0 during maximal exercise.

options.label: C
options.text: The V/P ratio is higher at the apex than at the base of the lungs when a person is standing.

options.label: D
options.text: Oxygen transfer can be explained by passive diffusion.

questions.answerText: The rate of alveolar ventilation at rest exceeds the rate of alveolar capillary perfusion.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) The rate of alveolar ventilation at rest exceeds the rate of alveolar capillary perfusion.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man visits his doctor because his wife has long complained of his snoring. He undergoes polysomnography and ventilatory response testing to ascertain the extent and cause of his sleep apnea. The activity of the central chemoreceptors is stimulated by which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: A decrease in the metabolic rate of the surrounding brain tissue

options.label: B
options.text: A decrease in the PO2 of blood flowing through the brain

options.label: C
options.text: An increase in the PCO2 of blood flowing through the brain

options.label: D
options.text: An increase in the pH of the CSF

questions.answerText: An increase in the PCO2 of blood flowing through the brain
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) An increase in the PCO2 of blood flowing through the brain

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman is participating in a controlled metabolic study. Her oxygen consumption is measured at 300 mL/min, and her carbon dioxide output is recorded as 270 mL/min. What is the estimated respiratory quotient (RQ) in this individual?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) 0.9

questions.stem: An anesthetized male is breathing with no assistance. He is then artificially ventilated for 10 min at his normal tidal volume but at twice his normal frequency. He is ventilated with a gas mixture of 60% O2 and 40% N2. The artificial ventilation is stopped & he fails to breathe for several minutes. This apneic episode is due to which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: High arterial PO2 suppressing the activity of the medullary chemoreceptors

options.label: B
options.text: Decrease in arterial pH suppressing the activity of the peripheral chemoreceptors

options.label: C
options.text: Low arterial PCO2 suppressing the activity of the medullary chemoreceptors

options.label: D
options.text: High arterial PCO2 suppressing the activity of the peripheral chemoreceptors

questions.answerText: Low arterial PCO2 suppressing the activity of the medullary chemoreceptors
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Low arterial PCO2 suppressing the activity of the medullary chemoreceptors

questions.stem: During acclimatization to high altitude all of the following take place except:

options.label: B
options.text: Increase in the sensitivity of central chemoreceptors

options.label: C
options.text: Increase in the sensitivity of carotid body to hypoxia

options.label: D
options.text: Shift in the oxygen dissociation curve to the left

questions.answerText: Shift in the oxygen dissociation curve to the left
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Shift in the oxygen dissociation curve to the left

questions.stem: A 12-year-old boy has a severe asthmatic attack with wheezing. He experiences rapid breathing and becomes cyanotic. His arterial PO₂ is 60 mm Hg and his PCO₂ is 30 mm Hg. Which of the following statements about this patient is most likely to be true?

options.label: A
options.text: Forced expiratory volume/forced vital capacity (FEV1/FVC) is increased

options.label: B
options.text: Ventilation/perfusion (V/Q) ratio is increased in the affected areas of his lungs

options.label: C
options.text: His arterial PCO₂ is higher than normal because of inadequate gas exchange

options.label: D
options.text: His arterial PCO₂ is lower than normal because hypoxemia is causing him to hyperventilate

questions.answerText: His arterial PCO₂ is lower than normal because hypoxemia is causing him to hyperventilate
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) His arterial PCO₂ is lower than normal because hypoxemia is causing him to hyperventilate

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following areas of nitrogen washout test indicate closing volume?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) IV

questions.stem: The parvocellular pathway from lateral geniculate nucleus to visual cortex is most sensitive for the stimulus of:
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Color contrast

questions.stem: The morning after a rock concert, a 20-year-old college student notices difficulty hearing his professor during lecture. The physician at the Student Health Center suspects possible damage to his hair cells by the loud music. Depolarization of the hair cells in the cochlea is caused primarily by the flow of which of the following?

options.label: C
options.text: Cl– out of the hair cell

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) K+ into the hair cell

questions.stem: For the eye to adapt to intense light, which of the following may occur?

options.label: A
options.text: Bipolar cells will continuously transmit signals at the maximum rate possible

options.label: B
options.text: Photochemical in both rods and cones will be reduced to retinal and opsins

options.label: C
options.text: There will be an increase in the size of the pupil

options.label: D
options.text: Vitamin A will convert into retinal

questions.answerText: Photochemical in both rods and cones will be reduced to retinal and opsins
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Photochemical in both rods and cones will be reduced to retinal and opsins

questions.stem: Maximum area in homunculus signifies which one of the following?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Increased preciseness of movements

questions.stem: A 53 year old male is brought to the emergency department with complains of right sided weakness and jargon speech. A CT brain was ordered to rule out haemorrhagic stroke. On neurological examination, there is normal object recognition but loss of comprehension. Which of the following areas is affected?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Superior temporal gyrus

questions.stemHtml: In a patient, the hypothalamic thermostat was reset from point V to point X as shown below. Which of the following happens in stage W compared to stage Y?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Shivering

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man loses his right hand in a farm accident. Four years later, he has episodes, of severe pain in the missing hand (phantom limb pain). A detailed PET scan study of his cerebral cortex might be expected to show:

options.label: A
options.text: Expansion of the right-hand area in his right primary somatosensory cortex.

options.label: B
options.text: Expansion of the right hand area in as left primary somatosensory cortex

options.label: C
options.text: Projection of fibers from neighbouring sensory areas into the right-hand area of his right primary somatosensory cortex.

options.label: D
options.text: Projection of fibers from neighbouring sensory areas into the right-hand area of his left primary somatosensory cortex.

questions.answerText: Projection of fibers from neighbouring sensory areas into the right-hand area of his left primary somatosensory cortex.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Projection of fibers from neighbouring sensory areas into the right-hand area of his left primary somatosensory cortex.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a component of the Papez circuit?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Posterior thalamic nuclei

questions.stem: Which neurotransmitter is primarily known for its facilitatory presynaptic and postsynaptic effects in CNS?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Glutamate

questions.stem: There is an area in the dominant hemisphere, which when damaged, might leave the sense of hearing intact but not allow words to be arranged into a comprehensive thought. Which of the following terms is used to identify this portion of the cortex?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Wernicke's area

questions.stem: Polyphagia in diabetes is mainly due to:

options.label: A
options.text: Decreased glucose utilization in most of the tissues of the body

options.label: B
options.text: Decreased glucose uptake by whole brain

options.label: C
options.text: Decreased glucose utilization by entire hypothalamus nuclei

options.label: D
options.text: Decreased glucose utilization of VMH causing less VMI activity.

questions.answerText: Decreased glucose utilization of VMH causing less VMI activity.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Decreased glucose utilization of VMH causing less VMI activity.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old female presents with chronic back pain & reports significant difficulty sleeping despite trying various over-the-counter sleep aids. She describes her pain as constant and throbbing, which worsens at night. Physical examination reveals tenderness over the lumbar spine & limited range of motion. Which of the following explains why individuals in severe pain have difficulty sleeping without sedative medication?

options.label: A
options.text: The somatosensory cortical area for pain perception blocks the sleep-generating circuits

options.label: B
options.text: Pain fibers entering the dorsal horn & the ascending pain pathways block the sleep-generating circuits

options.label: C
options.text: Ascending pain pathways provide excitatory input to brainstem reticular formation areas that are involved in maintenance of the alert, waking state

options.label: D
options.text: The neurotransmitters used in the slow pain pathway diffuse to neighboring cell groups & generally raise the excitability of the brain

questions.answerText: Ascending pain pathways provide excitatory input to brainstem reticular formation areas that are involved in maintenance of the alert, waking state
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Ascending pain pathways provide excitatory input to brainstem reticular formation areas that are involved in maintenance of the alert, waking state

questions.stemHtml: Identify the sleep wave marked in the EEG during sleep wake cycle:
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) REM Sleep

questions.stem: A 50-year-old male presents to the sleep clinic with complaints of excessive daytime sleepiness and frequent awakenings during the night. Polysomnography reveals multiple episodes of rapid eye movement (REM). Which of the following statements about REM sleep is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Although fast-wave sleep is frequently referred to as “dreamless sleep,” dreams and sometimes Night terrors do occur at this time

options.label: B
options.text: Individuals rarely will awaken spontaneously from REM sleep.

options.label: C
options.text: Muscle tone throughout the body is markedly suppressed during REM sleep

options.label: D
options.text: HR and respiratory rate typically become very regular during REM sleep

questions.answerText: Muscle tone throughout the body is markedly suppressed during REM sleep
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Muscle tone throughout the body is markedly suppressed during REM sleep

questions.stem: A 45-year-old patient visits a neurologist with a unique concern. The patient reports having difficulty recognizing familiar faces, including those of close family members and friends. This issue has been causing significant social discomfort. Which of the following conditions best describes the patient's symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Prosopagnosia

questions.stem: Which of the following is most likely not involved in production of LTP?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Membrane hyperpolarization

questions.stem: A 60-year-old male patient presents with excessive thirst and reduced urine output. Laboratory investigations reveal high ADH level and high urine osmolarity. What is the most likely physiological stimulus for his thirst?

options.label: A
options.text: Increases in plasma osmolality and volume.

options.label: B
options.text: An increase in plasma osmolality and a decrease in plasma volume.

options.label: C
options.text: A decrease in plasma osmolality and an increase in plasma volume.

options.label: D
options.text: Injection of vasopressin into the hypothalamus.

questions.answerText: An increase in plasma osmolality and a decrease in plasma volume.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) An increase in plasma osmolality and a decrease in plasma volume.

questions.stem: All of the following can be seen in lower motor neuron lesions, except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Hyperreflexia



lexia

questions.stem: All of the following are features of Brown-Séquard syndrome except:
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Contralateral dorsal column loss

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man is brought to the emergency room after a traffic accident causing a traumatic brain injury. Within several hours he begins eating objects such as paper, is unable to maintain attention, and displays increased sexual activity. He is diagnosed with Klüver-Bucy syndrome. A diagnostic MRI is ordered to confirm bilateral lesions of which of the following regions of the brain?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Temporal lobe

questions.stemHtml: Which is the main output neuron in the Image:
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Q

questions.stem: Many signaling pathways involve the generation of inositol trisphosphate (IP3) and diacylglycerol (DAG). These molecules:

options.label: D
options.text: Can activate calcium calmodulin-dependent protein kinases

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C)  Are derived from PIP2

questions.stem: Somatomedins mediates?

options.label: A
options.text: Deposition of chondroitin sulphate in bone for hypophyseal growth

options.label: D
options.text: Decreased rate of glucose uptake by cells

questions.answerText: Deposition of chondroitin sulphate in bone for hypophyseal growth
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Deposition of chondroitin sulphate in bone for hypophyseal growth

questions.stemHtml: The blood levels of a hormone are elevated during exercise and sleep as shown. Which hormone fits the description?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) GH

questions.stem: Through what “permissive action” do glucocorticoids accelerate gluconeogenesis during fasting?

options.label: A
options.text: Glucocorticoids stimulate the secretion of insulin, which activates gluconeogenic enzymes in the liver

options.label: B
options.text: Glucocorticoids inhibit the use of glucose by skeletal muscle

options.label: C
options.text: Glucocorticoids maintain the vascular response to norepinephrine

options.label: D
options.text: Glucocorticoids maintain the intracellular concentrations of many of the enzymes needed to carry out gluconeogenesis through effects on transcription

questions.answerText: Glucocorticoids maintain the intracellular concentrations of many of the enzymes needed to carry out gluconeogenesis through effects on transcription
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Glucocorticoids maintain the intracellular concentrations of many of the enzymes needed to carry out gluconeogenesis through effects on transcription

questions.stem: Which of the following is the primary action of inhibin?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) It inhibits secretion of FSH

questions.stem: Which of the following will decrease the secretion of insulin? HypokalemiaAcetylcholine GlucagonFasting
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) 1, 4

questions.stemHtml: During starvation, graph of three substances are plotted as below. The scale for A and B is on the left and the scale for C is on the right. Which of the substances are represented by the curve A?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) RT3

questions.stemHtml: A 50-year-old patient presents with symptoms of hyperparathyroidism. Laboratory analysis shows elevated levels of parathyroid hormone (PTH). The accompanying graph shows changes in plasma calcium and phosphate levels after administration of PTH. Which of the following mechanisms explains how PTH increases plasma calcium levels?

options.label: B
options.text: By promoting calcium absorption in the intestines

options.label: C
options.text: By increasing both osteoclastic activity and reducing renal calcium excretion

options.label: D
options.text: By enhancing phosphate absorption in the intestine

questions.answerText: By increasing both osteoclastic activity and reducing renal calcium excretion
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) By increasing both osteoclastic activity and reducing renal calcium excretion

questions.stem: Increasing intracellular I – due to the action of NIS is an example of:
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Secondary active transport

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding somatomedins is/are true? Somatomedins are produced primarily by the liver in response to growth hormone stimulation.The most important somatomedin is somatomedin C, also known as IGF-1.IGF-1 has a shorter half-life than growth hormone and is rapidly cleared from circulation.IGF-1 binds to carrier proteins in the blood, which prolong its half life The growth-promoting effects of growth hormone are largely due to the action of somatomedins on peripheral tissues.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) 1, 2, 4, 5 only

questions.stem: A manual labourer moves in March from hill station to a hot, tropical area and becomes acclimatized by working outdoors for a month. Compared with his responses on the first few days in the tropical area, for the same activity level after acclimatization one would expect higher:
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Sweating rate

questions.stem: In a kidney producing urine with an osmolality of 1,200 mOsm/kg H2O, the osmolality of fluid collected from the the cortical collecting duct is about:
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) 300 mOsm/kg H2O

questions.stem: In response to an increase in GFR, the proximal tubule and the loop of Henle demonstrate an increase in the rate of Na+ reabsorption. This phenomenon is called:
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Glomerulo tubular balance

questions.stem: Which of the following is/are the component(s) of the counter current multiplier of the countercurrent system? Descending limb of the loop of HenleThick ascending limb of HenleThin ascending limb of HenleVasa recta of the juxtamedullary nephron
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) 1, 2, 3

questions.stem: A patient has a creatinine clearance of 100 ml/ min, a plasma K+ concentration of 4.0 mmol/L, a urine flow rate of 2.0 m/ min, and a urine K+ concentration of 60 mmol/L What is his approximate rate of K+ excretion?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) 0.12 mmol/min

questions.stemHtml: In a patient with severe central diabetes insipidus caused by a lack of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) secretion, which part of the nephron would have the lowest tubular fluid osmolarity?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Segment E

questions.stem: If Glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure is 60 mmHg, Bowman’s capsule hydrostatic pressure is 15 and glomerular oncotic pressure is 30 and bowman’s capsule oncotic pressure is 5 the net filtration pressure will be________ mmHg.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) 20

questions.stem: Which of the following tends to decrease potassium secretion by the cortical collecting tubule?

options.label: B
options.text: A diuretic that decreases proximal tubule sodium reabsorption

options.label: C
options.text: A diuretic that inhibits the action of aldosterone (e.g., spironolactone)

questions.answerText: A diuretic that inhibits the action of aldosterone (e.g., spironolactone)
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) A diuretic that inhibits the action of aldosterone (e.g., spironolactone)

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man has a heart attack and experiences cardiopulmonary arrest while being transported to the emergency room. The following laboratory values are obtained from arterial blood: pH = 7.12, plasma PCO2 = 60 mmHg & HCO3− concentration = 19 mEq/L. Which of the following best describes his acid-base disorder?

options.label: A
options.text: Respiratory acidosis with partial renal compensation

options.label: B
options.text: Metabolic acidosis with partial respiratory compensation

options.label: C
options.text: Mixed acidosis: Combined metabolic and respiratory acidosis

options.label: D
options.text: Mixed alkalosis: Combined respiratory and metabolic alkalosis

questions.answerText: Mixed acidosis: Combined metabolic and respiratory acidosis
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Mixed acidosis: Combined metabolic and respiratory acidosis

questions.stem: A 50 years old obese and diabetic patient presented with frequent micturition. His BP was 170/90. His inulin clearance was 100 ml/ min. His plasma glucose was 400 mg/ dL. His TmG was 200 mg/min. Calculate his excreted load of glucose.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) 200 mg/min

questions.stem: Insulin increases the entry of glucose into:

options.label: B
options.text: The mucosa of the small intestine.

options.label: C
options.text: Most neurons in the cerebral cortex.

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Skeletal muscle.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding acid secretion and urine acidification is/are correct? The proximal tubule has maximum acid secretion.The collecting duct is the primary site of urine acidification.The minimum urinary pH is 4.5, which is the limiting pH.The distal convoluted tubule (DCT) is more involved in bicarbonate reabsorption than acid secretion.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) 1, 2 and 3 only

questions.stem: Which of the following graphs represent correct relationship between “mean arterial BP” and “plasma vasopressin (pmol/L)”?Abscissa= mean arterial BP ; Ordinate= plasma vasopressin
questions.solutionHtml: Ans C) C.

questions.stem: A nephrology resident is planning a research study to assess renal function in patients with suspected chronic kidney disease. The study aims to accurately determine the filtration fraction of the kidneys. Which combination of substances should be used to measure glomerular filtration rate (GFR) and renal plasma flow (RPF) for calculating the filtration fraction?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) PAH and inulin

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following statements is true regarding the given cystometrogram?

options.label: A
options.text: Segment l gives a significant urge for urination due to increase in pressure

options.label: B
options.text: Segment II is due to Laplace law

options.label: C
options.text: Micturition fails to happen in segment II

options.label: D
options.text: The dotted line represents that micturition has occurred

questions.answerText: Segment II is due to Laplace law
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Segment II is due to Laplace Law

questions.stem: Which of the following decreases GFR?

options.label: A
options.text: Increase in glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure

options.label: B
options.text: Decrease in Glomerular capillary oncotic pressure

options.label: D
options.text: Increase in Bowmans capsule hydrostatic pressure

questions.answerText: Increase in Bowmans capsule hydrostatic pressure
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Increase in Bowmans capsule hydrostatic pressure

questions.stemHtml: A nephrologist is explaining to medical students the concept of renal clearance and how different substances are handled by the nephron. Using the graph provided, she asks them to match substances with their typical clearance patterns. Identify the correctly matched pair of substances with their renal clearance from the graph:

options.label: A
options.text: A - Glucose, B - PAH, C - Bicarbonate, D - Inulin

options.label: B
options.text: A - Bicarbonate, B - Glucose, C Inulin -, D – PAH

options.label: C
options.text: A - PAH, B - Inulin, C - Glucose, D - Bicarbonate

options.label: D
options.text: A - Glucose, B - Bicarbonate, C - Inulin, D - PAH

questions.answerText: A - Glucose, B - Bicarbonate, C - Inulin, D - PAH
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) A - Glucose, B - Bicarbonate, C - Inulin, D – PAH

questions.stem: All of the following are true about secretin except:

options.label: A
options.text: It is secreted by S cells of intestine

options.label: B
options.text: It causes release of alkaline pancreatic juice rich in enzymes

options.label: C
options.text: Its action is mediated via intracellular cAMP

questions.answerText: It causes release of alkaline pancreatic juice rich in enzymes
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) It causes release of alkaline pancreatic juice rich in enzymes

questions.stem: A newborn boy does not pass meconium within 48 hours of delivery. His abdomen is distended, and he begins vomiting. A suction biopsy of a distally narrowed segment of the colon shows a lack of ganglionic nerve cells. The most probable diagnosis in this newborn is:
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Hirschsprung disease

questions.stem: A young man met with a motor bike accident and had injury to ileum and jejunum. Therefore the entire ileum and partial jejunum was resected. Which of the following would the patient suffer from?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Vitamin B12 deficiency

questions.stem: All except the following statements about short chain fatty acids in the colon are correct?

options.label: A
options.text: These fatty acids are produced in duodenum and absorbed in the colon.

options.label: B
options.text: They exert a trophic effect on the colonic epithelial cells.

options.label: C
options.text: They contribute significantly to the total caloric intake.

questions.answerText: These fatty acids are produced in duodenum and absorbed in the colon.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) These fatty acids are produced in duodenum and absorbed in the colon.

questions.stem: In a patient with chronic gastritis and peptic ulcer disease, it is important to understand the role of specific stomach cells. Which factor is primarily associated with enterochromaffin-like (ECL) cells of the stomach, and how does it contribute to the patient's condition?

options.label: A
options.text: Histamine, which stimulates gastric acid production, potentially exacerbating ulcer symptoms.

options.label: B
options.text: Gastrin, which promotes mucus production and provides protection against ulcers.

options.label: C
options.text: Pepsinogen, an enzyme involved in protein digestion within the stomach.

options.label: D
options.text: Secretin, a hormone that regulates pancreatic enzyme secretion, influencing digestion.

questions.answerText: Histamine, which stimulates gastric acid production, potentially exacerbating ulcer symptoms.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Histamine, which stimulates gastric acid production, potentially exacerbating ulcer symptoms.
